For $\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma ,\delta \in ℕ$, if $\int \left({\left(\frac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\frac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right){\log }_{e}xdx = \frac{1}{\alpha }{\left(\frac{x}{e}\right)}^{\beta x} - \frac{1}{\gamma }{\left(\frac{e}{x}\right)}^{\delta x} + C$, where $e = { \sum }_{n = 0}^{ \infty }\frac{1}{n!}$ and $C$ is constant of integration, then $\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 4\delta$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given,

$\int \left({\left(\frac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\frac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right)\ln xdx = \frac{1}{\alpha }{\left(\frac{x}{e}\right)}^{\beta x} - \frac{1}{\gamma }{\left(\frac{e}{x}\right)}^{\delta x} + C$

Now let $I = \int \left({\left(\frac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\frac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right)\ln xdx$

Now let {\left(\frac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} = t \implies 2x\left(\ln x - 1\right) = \ln t \implies \ln xdx = \frac{1}{2t}dt$

So, $I = \frac{1}{2} \int \left(t + \frac{1}{t}\right)\frac{dt}{t} \implies I = \frac{1}{2} \int \left(1 + \frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)dt \implies I = \frac{1}{2}\left(t - \frac{1}{t}\right) + c \implies I = \frac{1}{2}\left({\left(\frac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} - {\left(\frac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right) + C$

Now on comparing with $I = \frac{1}{\alpha }{\left(\frac{x}{e}\right)}^{\beta x} - \frac{1}{\gamma }{\left(\frac{e}{x}\right)}^{\delta x} + C$, we get $\alpha = 2,\beta = 2,\gamma = 2,\delta = 2$

Hence, $\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 4\delta = 2 + 4 + 6 - 8 = 4$

Hence this is the required option.

questions.explanation:
$\int \frac{\sin x}{{\sin }^{3}x + {\cos }^{3}x}dx = \alpha {\log }_{e} | 1 + \tan x | + \beta {\log }_{e}\left(1 - \tan x + {\tan }^{2}x\right) + \gamma {\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{2\tan x - 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + C,..........\left(i\right)$

Let, $I = \int \frac{\sin x}{{\sin }^{3}x + {\cos }^{3}x}dx I = \int \frac{\tan x{\sec }^{2}x}{{\tan }^{3} + 1}dx$

Put $\tan x = t \implies {\sec }^{2}xdx = dt = \int \frac{tdt}{{t}^{3} + 1} = \int \frac{t}{(t + 1)\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)}dt$

Now $\frac{t}{(t + 1)\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)} = \frac{A}{t + 1} + \frac{Bt + C}{{t}^{2} - t + 1} t = A\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right) + (Bt + C)(t + 1) t = {t}^{2}\left(A + B\right) - t\left(A - B - C\right) + A + C$

Comparing on both sides

$A + B = 0, - A + B + C = 1,A + C = 0$

Solving these equations

$A = - \frac{1}{3},B = \frac{1}{3},C = \frac{1}{3}$

Hence $I = \int \left(\frac{ - \frac{1}{3}}{t + 1} + \frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{t + 1}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}\right)\right)dt = - \frac{1}{3} \int \frac{1}{\left(t + 1\right)}dt + \frac{1}{3} \int \frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(2t - 1\right) + \frac{3}{2}}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}dt = - \frac{1}{3} \int \frac{1}{\left(t + 1\right)}dt + \frac{1}{6} \int \frac{2t - 1}{\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)} + \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{dt}{{\left(t - \frac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}^{2}} = - \frac{1}{3}\ln \left(t + 1\right) + \frac{1}{6}\ln \left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right) + \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}{\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{2t - 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + C = - \frac{1}{3}\ln \left(\tan x + 1\right) + \frac{1}{6}\ln \left({\tan }^{2}x - \tan x + 1\right) + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}{\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{2\tan x - 1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + C$

From equation $\left(i\right)$, Comparing from both sides

$\implies \alpha = - \frac{1}{3},\beta = \frac{1}{6}$ and $\gamma = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

So $18\left(\alpha + \beta + {\gamma }^{2}\right) = 18\left( - \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{3}\right) = 3$

questions.question: Let $I\left(x\right) = \int \frac{x + 1}{x{\left(1 + x{e}^{x}\right)}^{2}}dx,x > 0.$ If $\underset{x \to \infty }{\lim }I\left(x\right) = 0$ then $I\left(1\right)$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = \int \frac{x + 1}{x{\left(1 + x{e}^{x}\right)}^{2}}dx$

Now let $1 + x{e}^{x} = t \implies {e}^{x}\left(x + 1\right)dx = dt$

So, $I\left(x\right) = \int \frac{1}{\left(t - 1\right){t}^{2}}dt \implies I\left(x\right) = \int \frac{\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right) + {t}^{2}}{\left(t - 1\right){t}^{2}}dt \implies I\left(x\right) = \int \frac{ - \left(t + 1\right)}{{t}^{2}} + \frac{1}{t - 1}dt \implies I\left(x\right) = \int - \frac{1}{t} - \frac{1}{{t}^{2}} + \frac{1}{t - 1}dt \implies I\left(x\right) = - \ln t + \frac{1}{t} + \ln \left(t - 1\right) + C \implies I\left(x\right) = \ln \left(\frac{x{e}^{x}}{x{e}^{x} + 1}\right) + \frac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1} + C$

Also given,$\underset{x \to \infty }{\lim }I\left(x\right) = 0 \implies \underset{x \to \infty }{\lim }I\left(x\right) = \underset{x \to \infty }{\lim }\left(\ln \left(1 - \frac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1}\right) + \frac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1} + C\right) \implies \underset{x \to \infty }{\lim }I\left(x\right) = \left(\ln \left(1 - 0\right) + 0 + C\right) \implies C = 0$

Now finding,

$I\left(1\right) = \ln \left(\frac{e}{e + 1}\right) + \frac{1}{e + 1} = 1 + \frac{1}{e + 1} - \ln (e + 1) \implies I\left(1\right) = \frac{e + 2}{e + 1} - \ln \left(e + 1\right)$

questions.question: Let $I\left(x\right) = \int \sqrt{\frac{x + 7}{x}}dx$ and $I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7{\log }_{e}7$. If $I\left(1\right) = \alpha + 7{\log }_{e}\left(1 + 2\sqrt{2}\right),$ then {\alpha }^{4}$ is equal to _____.
questions.explanation:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = \int \sqrt{\frac{x + 7}{x}}dx$

Now let, $\frac{x + 7}{x} = {t}^{2} \implies - \frac{7}{{x}^{2}}dx = 2tdt \implies dx = \frac{ - 14t}{{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2}}dt$

So, $I\left(x\right) = - 14 \int \frac{{t}^{2}}{{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2}}dt \implies I\left(x\right) = - 14 \int \frac{dt}{\left({t}^{2} + \frac{1}{{t}^{2}} - 2\right)} \implies I\left(x\right) = \frac{ - 14}{2} \int \left(\frac{\left(1 - \frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)}{{\left(t + \frac{1}{t}\right)}^{2} - 4} + \frac{\left(1 + \frac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)}{{\left(t - \frac{1}{t}\right)}^{2}}\right)dt \implies I\left(x\right) = - 7\left(\frac{1}{4}\ln \left(\frac{t + \frac{1}{t} - 2}{t + \frac{1}{t} + 2}\right) - \frac{1}{t - \frac{1}{t}}\right) + c$

Now when $x = 9,t = \frac{4}{3} \implies I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7 \times \ln 7 = \frac{ - 7}{4}\ln {\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)}^{2} + 7 \times \frac{12}{7} + c \implies c = \frac{7}{2}\ln 7$

Now when $x = 1,t = 2\sqrt{2} \implies I\left(1\right) = + \frac{7}{4}\ln {\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2} + 1}{2\sqrt{2} - 1}\right)}^{2} + 7 \times \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{7} + \frac{7}{2}\ln 7 \implies I\left(1\right) = \frac{7}{2}\ln \left(\frac{{\left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}{7}\right) + 2\sqrt{2} + \frac{7}{2}\ln 7 \implies I\left(1\right) = 7\ln \left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right) - \frac{7}{2}\ln 7 + 2\sqrt{2} + \frac{7}{2}\ln 7 \implies \alpha = 2\sqrt{2} \implies {\alpha }^{4} = 64$

questions.question: If $\int \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \alpha {\log }_{e}\left(\cos 2x + \beta + \sqrt{\cos 2x\left(1 + \cos \frac{1}{\beta }x\right)}\right)$ + constant, then $\beta - \alpha$ is equal to ______.

$\int \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \alpha {\log }_{e}\left(\cos 2x + \beta + \sqrt{\cos 2x\left(1 + \cos \frac{1}{\beta }x\right)}\right) + C$

Now solving $L.H.S$ we get,

$\int \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \int \sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos 2x}{\cos 2x}}dx \implies \int \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sin x}{\sqrt{2{\cos }^{2}x - 1}}dx$

Now let $\cos x = t \implies - \sin xdx = dt \implies \int \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = - \sqrt{2} \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{2{t}^{2} - 1}} \implies \int \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = - \ln | \sqrt{2}\cos x + \sqrt{\cos 2x} | + C = - \frac{1}{2}\ln \left(2{\cos }^{2}x + \cos 2x + 2\sqrt{\cos 2x} \cdot \sqrt{2}\cos x\right) + C = - \frac{1}{2}\ln \left(\cos 2x + \frac{1}{2} + \sqrt{\cos 2x} \cdot \sqrt{1 + \cos 2x}\right) + C$

Now on comparing with $\int \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \alpha {\log }_{e}\left(\cos 2x + \beta + \sqrt{\cos 2x\left(1 + \cos \frac{1}{\beta }x\right)}\right) + C$

We get, $\beta = \frac{1}{2},\alpha = - \frac{1}{2} \implies \beta - \alpha = 1$
